info.name: EasyDora
info.description:
Executable documentation for EasyDora's main business flow (signup -> product -> order -> stock reservation -> payment -> notification), driven entirely through each service's public HTTP API. This collection complements docs/walkthrough.md -- it does not replace it. Every request here corresponds to a curl command already documented and verified in the walkthrough; where the two differ (e.g. this collection captures IDs/tokens automatically instead of showing them as shell variables), see postman/README.md for the exact mapping.

Run with the `Local` environment and the Collection Runner, top to bottom, with no manual steps in between.

item.name: Via Gateway (primary)
item.description: The Gateway (port 8080) is the primary entry point for this walkthrough, mirroring docs/walkthrough.md: every request here is identical to its 'Direct (debug)' counterpart except it goes through the Gateway with each service's own self-namespaced segment (/auth, /products, /orders, /billing, /inventory), which the Gateway forwards unchanged (ADR-0025). notification-service has no Gateway route yet, so its folder isn't duplicated here -- see 'Direct (debug)'.

item.description: GET /orders/fulfillment -- orders in PAYMENT_APPROVED, waiting to be shipped. No join, no seller scoping: an order can span more than one seller's products, so shipping is a platform-operations action, not a per-seller one.

item.name: Confirm Delivery
item.description: SHIPPED -> DELIVERED, ownership-gated exactly like Cancel Order -- only the order's own buyer can confirm receipt.

Mirrors docs/walkthrough.md step 12. Ship is a platform-operations action (role ADMIN, the first role-gated rather than ownership-gated endpoint in this project) since an order can span more than one seller's products; deliver stays ownership-gated like cancellation. See ADR-0029.

exec: pm.test('response is a non-empty array of notifications', function () {

item.description: notification-service's Gateway route (ADR-0026), self-namespaced the same way as every other service -- added after the frontend needed to reach this endpoint without calling the service directly. The bare direct-port route in the Direct (debug) section keeps working unchanged for the existing docs/walkthrough.md callers.

A real endpoint (PaymentService.processPayment) that exists in billing-service's code but is NOT part of docs/walkthrough.md's documented flow -- the walkthrough deliberately stops at PENDING (see docs/sequence-diagram.md's reading notes). Included here, clearly separated, because it's a real capability worth demonstrating, not because it's part of the core flow. The approval decision is delegated entirely to PaymentProvider (ADR-0030) -- deterministic, not random: 2 x this collection's fixed 249.90 product price = 499.80, not evenly divisible by 2, so this request always resolves to FAILED for this collection's fixed test data. Takes only orderId -- no amount parameter -- since it now always acts on the Payment row already created by order.created, never creating one itself (ADR-0031).

item.name: Cancel Order
item.description: Cancellable from PENDING/PROCESSING/INVENTORY_RESERVED (ADR-0029) -- this order is still early enough in its lifecycle immediately after creation. No endpoint for this existed anywhere in this collection before; the backend has always had it.

item.name: Verify Payment Exists (Compensation)

exec: pm.test('billing-service created a Payment row from order.created before we try to process it', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.description: billing-service creates this Payment row asynchronously, reacting to the same order.created event Create Order (Compensation) triggered -- calling Process Payment before this row exists returns 404 (ADR-0031: it now only ever acts on an already-created Payment, never creates one itself). Retry-polled the same way the main flow's Verify Payment Created already does.

item.name: Process Payment After Cancel (stray approval)

exec: pm.test('250.00 is evenly divisible by 2, so this deterministically approves', function () {

item.description: billing-service never checks the order's own state before approving a charge (ADR-0034) -- this call succeeds even though the order above was just cancelled, exactly reproducing the compensation scenario documented in docs/walkthrough.md.

item.name: Verify Order Refunded

exec: pm.test('orders-service detected the rejected PAYMENT_RECEIVED transition and moved to REFUNDING, then REFUNDED once billing-service published payment.refunded', function () {

item.description: Polls until REFUNDED. Needs a much larger retry budget than every other wait-loop in this collection (150, vs 8-10 elsewhere): reaching REFUNDED requires two additional RabbitMQ round trips beyond a normal state change (orders-service detecting the rejected transition -> payment.refund.requested -> billing-service deciding the refund -> payment.refunded back), and this loop has no real inter-retry delay (Postman's synchronous test-script model does not support setTimeout-based delays combined with pm.execution.setNextRequest), so only the retry count itself buys real wall-clock time.

Mirrors docs/walkthrough.md's "Payment compensation" section and ADR-0034. Self-contained: creates its own product/order (compensation_product_id/compensation_order_id) instead of reusing the main flow's order_id, so it can safely run after every earlier folder including 8. Final State without disturbing their already-asserted state. Requires an even, whole-dollar price (ADR-0030's deterministic payment provider) to reach APPROVED -- the collection's main flow price (249.90) never does, by design, which is why this scenario needs its own product.
